newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end down near lows after Dow drags.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end down near lows after Dow drags.

text.p: Australian shares finished weaker on Thursday, the market weighed down by a Wall Street fall after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan made cautionary comments at his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
The All Ordinaries index closed 18.4 points lower at 2,464.7, just off its intra-day low of 2,464.4.
"In summary, the market generally followed the Dow lower after some cautionary statements from Greenspan last night," said John Featherby, a dealer at Perth brokerage Hartley Poynton Ltd.

The dealer said the day's highlight was a deal by Newcrest Mining Ltd to sell its 11.9 percent stake in Normandy Mining Ltd to the Australia and New Zealand Banking Group under a two year equity gold swap arrangement.
Featherby said apart from this there were not too many other highlights with many investors using the weaker session as a buying opportunity in anticipation of further market gains.

Miner CRA, which reported its 1996 results after the market closed, went against the trend in climbing 7.6 cents to A$19.234 (US$14.81) as did fellow miner Pasminco which added seven cents to A$2.39 on the back of firmer base metals prices.

Foster's Brewing shares were busy with over 9.4 million shares traded, the bulk in options and dividend related trade prior to market opening. Its shares held their dividend, closing unchanged at A$2.73, after going ex-dividend five cents.
Capricorn Resources leapt 36 percent to finish at 30.5 cents after some encouraging assay results on Wednesday from its Roundtop nickel joint venture in Western Australia.

The flood of results continued with transport, health care and telecommunications group Mayne Nickless adding 11.2 cents to A$7.67 after reporting a 13.8 percent lower first half net profit of A$43.14 million.

Apart from the sale of its Normandy stake, Newcrest also announced that its half year operating earnings fell to A$8.52 million from A$21.74 million and said it expected to report lower earnings for the full year. Newcrest shares ended 1.8 cents weaker at A$4.882.
Optical products group OPSM Protector lost five cents to A$3.05, despite a 13.2 percent higher first half net profit of A$12.59 million.
Victorian-based totalisator betting agency Tabcorp dropped six cents to A$6.02 after posting a 17.5 percent higher first half net profit of A$51.21 million.
Gambling machine maker Aristrocrat Leisure lost a cent to A$3.02 after a first half net profit of A$8.27 million.
